rationale.oversight-explanation: Trust framework prescribes reasoning, citations, check visibility, and decision-ready analysis.
rationale.automation-bias: Java expert trusted hallucinated output throughout, despite explicit hallucination priming.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Participants required compilation plus unit, integration, deployment, and regression tests.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Developers reviewed, edited, corrected, approved, or rejected repository-wide AI changes.
rationale.survey-input: Study elicits substantive developer preferences for control, review, testing, and trust.
rationale.agentic: LLM migrates entire multi-file repositories, delivering artifact-level diffs for human review.
rationale.steering: Director role shapes generation through preferences, history, context, and feedback.
rationale.risk-quality: Study analyzes incomplete, incorrect, uncompilable outputs and testing-based quality mitigation.
rationale.risk-security: Trust framework includes vulnerability-introduction risk and security-check mitigation.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Observed expert persisted with hallucinated output until interviewer intervention.
rationale.method-self-report: Interviews and think-aloud commentary captured participant beliefs and preferences.
rationale.method-experiment: Developers were randomly assigned controlled successful or failed migration-review tasks.
